Custom Label Generation with SCALE 2021
The document field represents the document that you want the system to produce. All documents must be defined in the system under “document”.
Document Configuration
Document Type Configuration

Identifies the document as either a paper or label document. The document type required can be ‘shipping’ or ‘vendor’ for custom labels. All documents must be associated with a document type located under “document type” within configurations.
Document Routing Configuration

After you define a document, you need to provide its printing parameters on the Document Routing Window. The print parameters determine criteria such as: Ship to, Carrier, Container Class. Additionally, the routing determines number of copies, where the document is routed to, which document will be used, and what machine the document will print from.

Vendor Label

A vendor compliant label is a container identification label that is compliant with the ship to's specifications. 
If you would like to print both a container contents label and a vendor compliant label from the wave, see the topic Container Contents & Vendor Labels.
Printers producing vendor compliant labels must be accessible through a network share. Please refer to the Printer Configuration Guide for more information.
Shipping Label

A shipping label is used for carrier shipping purposes to identify a shipping container. It includes ship from and ship to information. The system automatically generates shipping labels during container packing and container manifesting. Note that if the shipping container is associated with a company, the system uses the company's name and address as the ship from values on this label.

NOTE** Show Carrier EDI Reference field configs
10
Container Contents Label

A container contents label identifies the items packed into a specific container. This label also includes such data as the item location, quantity, and basic shipment information. Container contents labels can be automatically printed during the container creation wave step. You can also manually print this label in the Shipping Container Insight (once the container has been packed).

Zebra Programming Language (ZPL)
What Is ZPL?

Zebra Programming Language

ZPL is a print language used by many label printers.  It is primarily used for labeling applications.

ZPL can be used to design label templates, as well as pull data from a SQL database.

Commonly used for interface error alerts or delete shipments.  
21
ZPL Command Basics

^XA – Start Format
^XZ – End Format
^FOx,y – field origin 
X – x coordinate
Y – y coordinate
^FS – field separator
^A0NX,Y – font size
X – width
Y – height
^FD – field data
^B% - barcode fonts
Bx, Bc, Bo, Bq, B3

^GB – graphic box
Other Commands

Wrap Text
^FB800,4,,,15
^A0N,30,40^FD  [[RECEIPT_DETAIL.ITEM_DESC]]^FS
Other Commands

Print Speed
^PR – sets print rate to a value that you specify
^PR12 vs ^PR8

Darkness
~SD – sets darkness to a value that you specify
^MD– adjusts the darkness relative to the current setting
Note: The ^MD is persistent across label formats until an new ^MD command is issued or the printer power is cycled.
Orientation
^FW – sets the default orientation for command fields
^FWr
R = rotate field;
N = normal, R = 90 degrees, I = 180 degrees, B = bottom-up 270 degrees

Client Cases
Client Case 1: Dish Break Label and Container Contents Label

Requirement: “We want to build our carts by container type.  We want our labels for parcel shipments to be grouped by container type while printing and we need to know how many of each container type will be used.  The users will be handed a stack of labels, starting with the break label, which will tell them how many of a specific container type are needed.  Then, they find the container types and then put them on a cart for picking.  We also need the Container ID barcoded.”
Resolution: We can configure our Label Master criteria to order our labels by Container Type, and can stamp the Container Type and count on Break Labels.  We can have a Break Label print for every Container Type. We will add a barcode to the top of the container contents label for the Container ID.

Client Case 2: Keeco LL Bean Vendor Label

Requirement: LL Bean requires a custom vendor label with very specific guidelines.  They are not a top 100 retailer, so Manhattan does not have the label developed.  The client asked the PSO team to assist with development.
Resolution:  Use the generic vendor label as a template and then edit it to match the requirement.  Use the ^GB command to draw out the lines needed on the label and then input the necessary field commands.

Client Case 3: Dish Customer Returns Label

Requirement: Dish needs an LPN label for each item that is returned.  The items are small, so they need a 2x3 version of the receipt container label to print during check in.  The label needs to print horizontally as well.
Resolution:  Use label lary to format the label with a 2x3 size, and use the ^FW command to rotate the label 90 degrees.
